names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Παυσίκακος Επίσκοπος Συνάδων», with the rank word and the see left off.

death.note: saint.gr gives no year of death and says only «Απεβίωσε ειρηνικά, μοχθώντας για την επισκοπή του μέχρι τελευταίας του πνοής»; the bracket here is what the page's own two reigns allow — he lived «στα χρόνια του βασιλιά Μαυρικίου (582 - 602 μ.Χ.)» and was made bishop by the patriarch Kyriakos «(595 - 606 μ.Χ.)», so his episcopate begins no earlier than 595.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Παυσίκακος Επίσκοπος Συνάδων»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **Nothing in the corpus reads as him**: the namesweep printed no row for the name at all. **`physician` is in `types`** on the page's own «σπούδασε όχι μόνο Θεολογία, αλλά και ιατρική για να την εξασκήσει δωρεάν υπέρ των φτωχών» — he studied medicine to practise it free for the poor — and on the emperor Maurice's cure. **The `dates` bracket is the page's own two reigns and nothing else**, and its `note` says so; the page gives no year of birth or death. **No `locations` object**, although Apamea in Bithynia and Synada are named. No hymn is printed; the page's couplet promises a strange ceasing of ills to whoever runs to his relic.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
